passage:
Damini: hi Yogesh, sorry to bother you on leave. I've taken over the vendor payments sheet
Yogesh: no worries! what's up
Damini: there's a row marked "hold" with no note. do I pay or not?
Yogesh: oh that one. hold until they send the corrected invoice
Damini: ok. and which is the real final file, "final_v3_new" or the other one?
Yogesh: v3_new. ignore the rest
Damini: also the sheet says "call Mr. Rao" and I don't know who that is or why 😅
Yogesh: Rao is at the bank. he approves transfers above the usual limit, needs a call first
Damini: would have been good to know before I paid one on Monday
Yogesh: oh no, sorry. let's write it all on one page today 🙏

qa.q: What was the row marked "hold" waiting for?
qa.a: It was waiting for the corrected invoice.

qa.q: What was Damini feeling on finding rows and files with no explanation?
qa.a: Confused and a bit anxious, unsure what to pay or whom to call.

qa.q: What small step could Yogesh and Damini take now?
qa.a: Write everything on one page today: the holds, the correct file and Mr. Rao's role.

qa.q: How does Yogesh react on hearing about Monday's payment?
qa.a: Apologetic and concerned, offering to write it all down straight away.

grounding: Shows a colleague inheriting unfinished work with missing context and unknown risks, and having to reconstruct it.

passage: When Irawati was posted to another block, Vidya took over the ledger at the village seed store. Some entries carried only initials. Three farmers were marked "as agreed". A cupboard was locked with no key in sight, and one phone number had no name beside it. Irawati was on a bus with poor signal. Vidya spent two days going door to door asking what had been agreed, guessed wrongly twice, and gave one farmer the wrong quantity. She did not blame Irawati. Instead she started a new page headed "what I know, what I don't" and sent it over. Irawati's answers came back the next evening.

qa.q: How many days did Vidya spend asking around?
qa.a: Vidya spent two days going door to door.

qa.q: What was Vidya feeling while rebuilding the ledger?
qa.a: Uncertain and pressed, worried about making more mistakes.

qa.q: What could Vidya do to cut down on guessing?
qa.a: Write a page of what she knows and what she doesn't and send it to Irawati, as she did.

qa.q: How might Irawati have felt on getting Vidya's page?
qa.a: Probably regretful about the missing details but glad to help, since Irawati sent answers back the next evening.

grounding: Shows a colleague inheriting half-known work with unclear entries and missing keys, losing time and making mistakes through no fault of her own.

passage:
On Monday Madhav took over the Gurugram client's brochure from Sudha, who had moved to another team overnight. Her handover was one line in an email: "Files in shared drive. Client is happy. Nearly done."
The shared drive had eleven versions: final, final_v2, final_client, FINAL_use_this. Two used different logos. There was a comment in one file, "Check with Rajiv re price table?", and no answer anywhere.
Madhav spent the morning opening files and comparing them. He tried to call Sudha, but she was in back-to-back meetings. The client wanted it by Wednesday.
He picked the newest-looking version and sent it on Tuesday. On Wednesday the client replied: "This is the old price table. We changed this two weeks ago."
Madhav stared at the email, jaw tight. He had worked late for two days, and still he had guessed wrong, with no way to have known.

qa.q: How many versions did the shared drive have?
qa.a: The shared drive had eleven versions.

qa.q: How did Madhav feel reading the client's reply?
qa.a: Madhav felt frustrated and stung, jaw tight, having worked late only to guess wrong without the missing context.

qa.q: What would have helped Madhav at the start?
qa.a: A handover naming the current file, the open question about the price table, and a short call with Sudha.

qa.q: How might the client see the mistake?
qa.a: The client probably sees the team as careless, not knowing the error came from a handover with missing context.

grounding: Shows a colleague inheriting an unfinished task with missing context and unclear decisions, forced to guess, and blamed for a mistake that was not his fault.

passage:
"Harsha, got two minutes? It's about the conference."
"Sure, Rukmini. How's it going?"
"Honestly? I'm lost. Your handover said 'venue sorted.' Which venue? There are emails with two hotels."
"The one by the lake. I told them yes on the phone."
"On the phone. So there's no written booking?"
"Ah. No. I was going to email."
"Okay. And the catering? The spreadsheet says 'vegan?' with a question mark."
"Someone asked. I didn't decide."
"And the speaker from Pune? The file says 'maybe.'"
"She confirmed on a call last Friday."
Rukmini put her pen down. "Harsha, I spent all of yesterday guessing. I nearly booked the other hotel."
"I'm really sorry. It all felt settled in my head."
"Can you send me everything you decided on calls, today? With who you spoke to?"
"Yes. By four."
"Thank you." She let out a breath. "I was starting to think I was the problem."

qa.q: What did Harsha's handover say about the venue?
qa.a: Venue sorted.

qa.q: How had Rukmini been feeling before this talk?
qa.a: Rukmini felt lost and anxious, having spent a day guessing and starting to think she was the problem.

qa.q: What request from Rukmini will help most, and why?
qa.a: Asking Harsha to send everything decided on calls, with names, by four, because those decisions existed only in Harsha's memory.

qa.q: How does Harsha feel when he hears about the other hotel?
qa.a: Harsha feels sorry and embarrassed, admitting it all felt settled in his head.

grounding: Illustrates a colleague inheriting half-known work, with unrecorded decisions and open questions, who loses time guessing through no fault of her own.

passage:
When Anjali went on maternity leave in March, I took over the school's admissions data. Her note said, "Mostly done. A few pending." I'm Seema, and I thought "a few" meant a few.
There were thirty-eight pending files. Some had a pencil tick I didn't understand. Some had a sticky note: "call back." Call who back? About what? The spreadsheet had a column called "status 2" with no heading explanation.
I spent two weeks reconstructing. I called parents who had already been called. One family got two admission letters with different fees. I rang them, apologised and felt my face burn.
I didn't want to disturb Anjali with a new baby. So I guessed, and some of my guesses were wrong.
Looking back, it wasn't carelessness on either side. Anjali was tired and rushing; the knowledge was in her head. I was trying hard. The gap between us is where the mistakes grew.

qa.q: How many pending files were there?
qa.a: There were thirty-eight pending files.

qa.q: How did Seema feel after the family got two admission letters?
qa.a: Seema felt embarrassed and guilty, face burning while apologising for a mistake born from guessing.

qa.q: What could have made this handover work better?
qa.a: A list of the pending files with what each tick, note and column meant, plus a short walk-through before the leave began.

qa.q: How might Anjali feel if she heard about the two letters?
qa.a: Anjali might feel sorry and a little guilty, since the missing context was knowledge she had carried in her head.

grounding: Shows a colleague inheriting unfinished work with missing context, losing time and making mistakes that are not the receiver's fault.

passage:
Supervisor's note, site office, Thursday.
Raghav has spent four days on the drainage drawings Jagdish left when he moved to the Pune project. Today I watched him with three versions of the same plan open, trying to work out which one the client approved. The file names say only "final", "final2" and "use this". A pipe size is crossed out in pencil with no reason written. Raghav rang Jagdish twice; Jagdish is on site all day and didn't pick up.
Raghav chose "final2" and ordered the site levels on that basis. By evening we found the client had signed "use this". Two days of levels to redo. He sat with his head in his hands for a while, then said quietly, "I did the best with what I had." He did.
Next steps: I have booked a one-hour call with Jagdish for tomorrow and told Raghav in writing that the delay is not on him.

qa.q: Which version had the client actually signed?
qa.a: The client had signed "use this".

qa.q: What does Raghav sitting with his head in his hands suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: It suggests he felt discouraged and frustrated at losing two days of work, even though he knew he had done the best with what he had.

qa.q: What could have prevented the lost days?
qa.a: A handoff note saying which file the client approved and why the pipe size changed, plus a short call before Jagdish moved, would have removed the guessing.

qa.q: How does the supervisor see Raghav's mistake?
qa.a: The supervisor sees it as not Raghav's fault, agreeing "He did" and putting in writing that the delay is not on him.

grounding: Shows a colleague taking over unfinished work with missing context and unclear decisions, losing time through no fault of their own.
